rationale: The empty static profile (no source lines, unknown function set) indicates a small, class-driven C++ benchmark (Prolangs-C++ office) with likely short, call-heavy functions and no hot numeric kernels, so the table biases toward transformations with strong resistance-per-cost: SUB and SPLIT are nearly free and are weighted to apply broadly; ICALL and IBR get high security/diversity weights because C++ virtual-heavy code tolerates indirection well and they defeat static call-graph recovery, with moderate runtime-cost weights to keep the compiler from applying them to obviously hot functions; FLA receives the highest SecurityGain since control-flow flattening is the strongest structural deterrent, but its elevated RuntimeCost weight (0.7) restricts it to functions whose features indicate low execution frequency; BCF is enabled moderately with raised SizeCost (0.6) because its bogus-block bloat matters more in a small binary; and IGV is kept at the lowest security weight with the highest CorrectnessRisk weight (0.4) since global-variable indirection offers the least resistance here and carries the most risk in C++ with static initialization and ODR-sensitive globals — the net effect maximizes layered reverse-engineering resistance while letting the cost dimensions gate the expensive passes on this size- and latency-sensitive small binary.
